Label: accountability as the dual back-edge
Description: The reading of accountability as the dual (star) back-edge to trust: for every forward commitment there is a return edge along which responsibility can be traced, so accountability is the *-dual that makes the trust structure two-way. Whether this pairing is merely a duality (an involution) or a full adjunction (with unit and counit) is an open fork recorded in `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`; the [accountability-dual-edge]--dual-to--[trust-enriched-hom] edge encodes the conservative reading. It is a member of the [praxis-nexus] region.

Label: the anthropic anchor (non-invertibility of the counit)
Description: The reading of the counit of [cross-site-adjunction] as non-invertible: the passage from the running community back to pure perspective loses information and cannot be undone, which is where "the human" — the contingent, the situated — enters and cannot be abstracted away. Its irreversibility is a feature: it blocks a God's-eye collapse, aligning with the refusal of any total self-view (see [lawvere-diagonal]). This is one member of the [anchors] region.

Label: care as an order-two involution (Peircean agape)
Description: A transverse structure, not one of the four adjoint parts: an order-two involution — a dualising, self-inverse operation — that we read as Peirce's agape, the "anti-managerial affect" that lets independent inquirers stay independent while remaining open to common truth. It is a *condition on* the community rather than a *product of* it, so in dependency order it sits upstream of the verification machinery. "Care" is our plain-English image; the structural content is the involution. This is one member of the [anchors] region.

Label: complexity as the left adjoint
Description: The reading of the left adjoint (Allow) of [cross-site-adjunction] as the direction of increasing complexity: modal perspectives unfold into the richer, more differentiated running community. Free / left-adjoint constructions generate "the most general world in which given material can live", which matches the intuition that complexity is produced, not presupposed. This is one member of the [anchors] region.

Label: evolution as the right adjoint
Description: The reading of the right adjoint (Require) of [cross-site-adjunction] as the direction of evolutionary reflection: the running community's operational separation is reflected back as constraints the perspectival type theory must satisfy. Right adjoints preserve limits and extract invariants, which matches the intuition of selection and conserved structure. This is one member of the [anchors] region.

Label: praxis as the adjunction unit
Description: The reading of the unit of [cross-site-adjunction] as praxis: the natural transformation by which a context enters its own running realisation and returns changed. It is the categorical home, at the level of the whole framework, of the "borrow – work – give back" cycle named in [logic-as-contextual-transformation]. This is one member of the [anchors] region.

Label: auditability theorem
Description: Auditability: for every state transition of the system there exists an audit certificate explaining why that transition was allowed, so every accepted change can be replayed and independently checked. It is the "no opaque decision path" guarantee — the theorem that closes off hidden bureaucracy by making the reason for every move part of the public record. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is what turns the trace from a log into something a stranger can re-derive rather than take on faith.

Label: Belyi's theorem and dessins d'enfants (with the icosahedral–E₈ theme)
Description: Belyi's theorem — a smooth projective curve is defined over a number field iff it admits a map to the projective line ramified only over {0, 1, ∞} — together with its combinatorial traces, the dessins d'enfants (bipartite graphs on surfaces). It is the paradigm "trace-compiler": a childlike finite mark carrying deep arithmetic (Galois) structure, which is what the community's trace layer aspires to. We fold in the allied theme that a small symmetry can unfold into an exceptional structure — the alternating group A₅ (icosahedral symmetry), through the binary icosahedral group and the McKay correspondence, reaching the E₈ lattice (Baez). It is the concrete instance behind [esquisse-trace-mathematics]; see `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: catalytic factorization (territory ⊗ explorer → book ⊗ explorer)
Description: The reading of exploration as a catalytic factorization: a territory together with an explorer is transformed into a book (a chart) together with the same explorer — the explorer is borrowed and returned unchanged, while the territory is what does the work of becoming charted. The "geographer" is the plain-English image (after Saint-Exupéry). Because the catalyst is conserved across the reaction, this is a clean instance of "borrow – work – give back", and its 0-truncation into a buildable artifact links it to the chart/book side of practice. It instantiates [logic-as-contextual-transformation]; see `workflow/arc/13_catalysts_and_care.md`.

Label: bulk/boundary as Isbell–Gelfand duality (Chu construction)
Description: The resolution of the framework's bulk/boundary problem as a duality: Isbell / Gelfand duality — with the Connes noncommutative face — between a space and its algebra of functions, realised concretely as a Chu construction with "reality-points" on one side, "documentation-states" on the other, paired by a lossy evaluation into a dualising object k. This is explicitly *not* a holographic identification of bulk with boundary; it is a duality *with loss*, which is exactly why documentation can chart reality without enclosing it. Taken from `workflow/arc/11_reality.md`, where it also carries the open conjecture that the outer dualising object k might coincide with an inner session-orthogonality; the codebase holds it as the Chu and session-Chu models.

Label: cobordism, dualizable objects, and the TFT–CFT–QFT ladder
Description: The bridge from typed traces to physics: a field theory read as a machine that assigns data to contexts (boundaries) and to transformations between them (cobordisms), with gluing as composition. The cobordism hypothesis is the hinge — fully dualizable objects classify fully extended framed topological field theories — which formalises the framework's "flip of perspective" as the coherent duality (evaluation/coevaluation) an object must carry. Adding geometry, scale, and local observables (factorization algebras) climbs the ladder from topological to conformal to quantum field theory. It is a compositional, dualizable instance of [recursive-context-articulation]; see `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: collective-memory theorem
Description: Collective memory: if a claim was rejected, repaired, deprecated, or superseded, then any future reuse must carry that status unless a valid repair or translation is supplied — the system remembers its failures. It is one of the most practically consequential members, turning the trace into an institution that does not silently relitigate settled errors or resurrect refuted claims. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it rests directly on [provenance], since remembering a claim's fate requires its lineage to be intact.

Label: the concurrent Community of Inquirers (actor-causal leg)
Description: The community side: a Peircean Community of Inquirers realised as a concurrent actor system in which all inquirers share one type ("unityped actors") and only the traces of their interaction are richly typed — the design law is "type moves, not people". It draws on Peirce's community-of-inquiry and agapism, Hewitt's actor model, and session-typed concurrency (Caires–Pfenning). Verification is mechanised (proof assistants as a public discharge organ) so that no human class monopolises checking, and the rules are themselves editable through the same typed traces. It supplies the right-hand site of [cross-site-adjunction] and is the locus of the `practice` perspective. See `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md` and `workflow/deep_context/concurrency_anchor.md`.

Label: conservative self-editing theorem
Description: Conservative self-editing: a proposed change to the system's own rules either preserves prior verified results under translation, or explicitly marks which results are invalidated, migrated, or made context-bound. It is what lets the community edit itself without silently destroying its past, and so it is the theorem that makes reflexive self-governance safe rather than reckless. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is the condition under which the community's self-editability — a defining feature of the concurrent leg — does not become a way to erase inconvenient history.

Label: the constitutive exterior (reality present-by-absence)
Description: The framework's outer pole: an exterior — what it calls "reality" — that is never made an internal sort, and is present only negatively, through the disciplines it imposes (unityping, non-enactment, availability-only access, buffered entry). It is the thing the recursion explores and forms perspectives on but never encloses; treating it as an internal object would be the characteristic error the design guards against. It is the outer face of [openness-at-both-ends] (the inner face being the universe hierarchy). See `workflow/arc/11_reality.md`.

Label: creativity-admissibility theorem
Description: Creativity admissibility: a new type, language, or context-extension is admissible when it resolves a typed obstruction, preserves the required prior structure, and opens verified new constructions — creative rule-change is allowed, but must leave a trace of why it was needed and what it preserves. It is the family's formal room for innovation without arbitrary rule-breaking, the place where the free leap stays answerable to what it forgets. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it presupposes both the [creativity-transition-operator] it disciplines and the [obstruction] its admissibility criterion refers to.

Label: creativity as the context-transition operator
Description: Creativity given a formal home as the operator that carries one context-and-logic to another, rather than as an inference inside a fixed one. Its micro-logic is Peircean abduction (proposing a new type for what had no place in the old grammar); its rhythm is Lautmanian saturation then liberation; its categorical image is the free / left-adjoint leap answerable to what it forgets. It is transformational in Boden's sense: it changes the space of possibilities, and so cannot be fully domesticated inside any one formalism — it becomes visible only after producing the form that makes it visible. It is the operator form of the passage in [recursive-context-articulation]; see `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: cross-site adjunction between the modal-HoTT topos and the concurrency/actor category
Description: The central conjectured object: an adjoint pair between the modal-homotopy-type-theory side [modal-cohesive-hott] and the concurrent-community side [concurrent-community-of-inquirers], written in project notation as Allow ⊣ Require. The left adjoint (Allow) unfolds modal perspectives into a running community; the right adjoint (Require) reflects the community's operational separation back into perspectival type theory. It is modelled on Lawvere's "unity and identity of opposites" / adjoint-cylinder reading of dialectics and on cohesion's adjoint modalities. An earlier three-slot version, with a middle "Mediate", is recorded in the now-largely-stale `workflow/naming.md`; the current reading is the pair, with the middle-slot question left open. This is the single object the whole conjecture is about.

Label: the dagger-compact / cartesian no-go
Description: The no-go theorem that a nontrivial dagger-compact category cannot be cartesian, used here as a forcing constraint: it means the framework's two sides cannot be collapsed into one, because a self-dual, linear, conserved, non-copyable regime (the concurrency / process side) is provably incompatible with a cartesian, intuitionistic, copyable, directed regime (the perspectival type-theory side). So the separation of concerns is not a design preference but a theorem — you cannot have both free copyability and genuinely conserved, non-copyable resources in one category. Drawn from `workflow/arc/13_catalysts_and_care.md`; it is why [cross-site-adjunction] must bridge two different categories rather than live inside one, and why the conserved base of the praxis nexus can exist at all.

Label: the enriched-completion setting (quantale / *-autonomous + Isbell completion)
Description: The formal home of the praxis nexus: the type-diagnosis graph dynamics modelled as a category enriched in a quantale / *-autonomous base, together with its Cauchy / reflexive (Isbell) completion. In this setting "openness" — treating the foreign as one's own — is exactly reflexive completeness, which coincides with representability, which is what [legitimacy-representability] reads as legitimacy. It supplies the ambient structure the [praxis-nexus] members share, and is built over the conserved base [risk-linear-base]. See `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`.

Label: the Grothendieck origin-mapping (seed, not foundation)
Description: The historical seed of the whole project: three of Grothendieck's late writings mapped onto its three pillars — *Pursuing Stacks* onto the modal-HoTT side, *Esquisse d'un Programme* onto the concurrency side, and *Récoltes et Semailles* onto the motivation/praxis — recorded at the opening of the arc (arc file 01). It is deliberately given few logical edges: it is where the project *came from*, not what it *rests on*, and treating the origin as a foundation is exactly the seductive error the framework warns against (its start is a produced fixed point, not a given ground — see the `must-not-glue-to` edge to [initiality-bootstrap]). Its one structural role is self-referential: the founding of Hoapa is itself an instance of a context producing a new language.

Label: the Esquisse constellation as trace mathematics
Description: The cluster of tools from Grothendieck's *Esquisse d'un Programme* — Grothendieck topologies / sites, sheaves and stacks, moduli, descent, tame ("moderated") topology, dévissage, and the "principle of anodyne choices" — read as the mathematics of how small local traces reconstruct hidden global structure. We propose it, conjecturally, as the natural architecture for the verification/trace layer of [concurrent-community-of-inquirers], because that layer needs exactly local-to-global assembly, presentation-invariance, and descent. It is a meta-module: a named toolkit rather than a single theorem, gathered in `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: fork/merge safety theorem
Description: Fork/merge safety: if two inquiry branches agree on their overlap and their obligations are compatible, then their merge is well-typed and preserves the results each branch verified. It is what lets a community disagree productively — compatible divergences recombine without corrupting the trace — and categorically it is where pushouts, colimits, descent, and sheaf-like gluing enter. As a member of the [protocol-theorems] region it therefore presupposes the [esquisse-trace-mathematics], the toolkit that supplies exactly that gluing discipline.

Label: the incubator convergence (care fixed point = Chu points = bootstrap)
Description: The point where three threads of the construction turn out to coincide: the "incubator" — the place where new inquirers and new contexts are brought into being — is at once the fixed point of the care involution [anchor-care], a "points" construction from [chu-isbell-duality], and the initiality / free-model bootstrap [initiality-bootstrap]. That these three are one object is one of the arc's convergences (`workflow/arc/13_catalysts_and_care.md`): what appears as an ethical condition (care), a semantic construction (Chu points), and a foundational move (initiality) are three descriptions of a single self-stabilising thing. "Incubator" is our plain-English image for that shared fixed point; its interest is that it makes the framework's ethics, semantics, and foundations meet at one place rather than run in parallel.

Label: the initiality / free-model bootstrap
Description: The framework's answer to "where does it start", given that it forbids a first instant or a foundational floor: it starts from a *fixed point* rather than a ground — secure bases are "produced, not given", via initiality / free-model (initial-algebra) universal properties that let a context bootstrap its own secure structure. This is the surprising temporal inversion: the nearest thing to an entry point is a self-stabilising fixed point of [recursive-context-articulation], not a base on which the rest is built. See `workflow/arc/11_reality.md` and the free ⊣ forgetful avatar of [cross-site-adjunction].

Label: Lawvere's fixed-point theorem (diagonal argument)
Description: Lawvere's fixed-point theorem in a cartesian-closed category: if an object weakly parametrises all maps into an object B, then every endomap of B has a fixed point; contrapositively, a fixed-point-free operation on B (such as negation) makes such total self-parametrisation impossible. It is the categorical generalisation of Gödel incompleteness and Tarski undefinability. In the framework it is the "anti-sovereignty" result: no sufficiently expressive, self-editing community can hold a complete internal account of its own verification, so the system must stay open, stratified, and self-revising. It is also the precise content of the single asymmetry on which the conjecture's "if" turns — a category rich in fixed points versus one poor in them — which is why the [cross-site-adjunction] has a direction rather than being a symmetric equivalence.

Label: legitimacy as earned representability
Description: The reading of legitimacy as earned universality: a contribution or authority is legitimate when it is representable — determined by the total pattern of its relations rather than by an intrinsic privilege — which in the enriching setting coincides with reflexive (Isbell) completeness. Its two concrete grounds are "no-leak" (renaming-invariance) and initiality [initiality-bootstrap], so legitimacy is produced, not granted. It is a member of the [praxis-nexus] region and is an instance of the property named in [enriched-completion-setting]. See `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`.

Label: the '!' (bang) modality as verification (Benton linear/non-linear adjunction)
Description: The reading of the exponential "!" (the "bang" modality) as verification, modelled by a Benton linear/non-linear adjunction F ⊣ G between a cartesian world and a linear one: G archives (a linear resource becomes a reusable value), F deploys (a reusable value re-enters linear use), and ! = GF is the comonad whose coalgebras are the freely-reusable, verified objects — a "passage to a reusable form". We take it from `workflow/arc/13_catalysts_and_care.md`. Crucially it is an adapter *internal to the concurrency leg*, a discipline on how linear traces become reusable; the arc's grounding pass insists it must not be conflated with the cross-site adjunction (nor "!" with a buffer, nor this passage with descent) — see the `must-not-glue-to` edge to [cross-site-adjunction].

Label: liveness theorem
Description: Liveness: under fair participation and bounded obligations, every valid proposal eventually reaches a definite status — accepted, rejected, forked, deferred, or obstructed — so the system cannot bury a valid contribution forever. It is what stops managerial delay from reappearing as procedural inertia: where the other members of the [protocol-theorems] region constrain *what* is accepted, liveness constrains *that a decision is reached at all*. A member of the family, it is the safety-versus-progress complement to soundness.

Label: logic as valid transformation under context
Description: The framework's account of what logic is: not primarily inference over propositions, but the disciplined act of borrowing from a context, performing work, and discharging the dependency as a reusable form — the image is "borrow – work – give back". Its sharpest proof-theoretic picture is Gentzen–Prawitz–Dummett introduction/elimination with assumption discharge, but the same structure is recovered from Tarskian model theory, Girard's linear logic, category-theoretic internal logic, and Dewey's logic-as-inquiry (all surveyed in `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`). We treat it as the inner engine of [recursive-context-articulation]: the metaphysics says worlds are made by typed transformations of context; this node says which transformations are valid. "Borrow – work – give back" is our plain-English image for the five-moment cycle dependency → use → transformation → discharge → recontextualisation.

Label: the colimit of logic-neighbours
Description: A forcing-colimit, not a shape: the diagram of established positions whose shared shape forces the framework's notion of logic, [logic-as-contextual-transformation]. Dewey (logic as inquiry), Girard (linear/resource logic), Lawvere (internal logic of a topos), Martin-Löf (constructive inhabitation), Abramsky (contextuality, failed gluing), Pym–O'Hearn (bunched/separation logic, non-collapsing local work), and Goguen–Burstall institution theory (networks of logics and their translations). It is the inner-engine counterpart to [philosophy-neighbour-colimit]: no single author states the whole, but each fixes one facet of "valid transformation under context", and the [logic-as-contextual-transformation] `forced-by` edge into this node carries that derivation. The logic pendulum's equilibrium seed [workilibrium-logic] is *not* this colimit: per "shapes vs forcing-colimits" the forcing stays here, at the colimit level, even once the logic pendulum is drawn — never migrating onto the equilibrium node alone.

Label: Grothendieck — the cared-for working balance
Description: Grothendieck read at the equilibrium as the cared-for working balance: the "rising sea" method in which one does not force a problem but patiently builds the right context — the topos, the scheme, the relative point of view — until the problem dissolves of itself. This is the mathematical exemplar of the pendulum's orthogonal working plane: the polemic between Lawvere's form and Lautman's problem is metabolised into an ongoing practice of context-construction held with care, not resolved on the pole-axis. It ties directly to the framework's own trace-mathematics and to [recursive-context-articulation] via [pendulum-recontextualization], where the built context becomes the ground of the next problem.

Label: Lautman — the demand for novelty
Description: Lautman read at the right pole as the demand for novelty: a dialectic of Ideas in which problems and their tensions govern the solutions that mathematics invents — the genetic side where the not-yet-formed problem is primary and structure is its precipitate. His two movements, saturation and liberation (the `saturates`/`liberates` edge-type takes its name here), are the characteristic gestures of this pole. Read with Zalamea as commentator. Held in tension with [mathematics-lawvere] by [pendulum-poles-polemic] and discharged toward the working plane by [pendulum-stabilization].

Label: Lawvere — the demand for form
Description: Lawvere read at the left pole as the demand for form: the drive to internalise logic and structure categorically — adjoint functors as a precise "unity of opposites", the elementary topos as a world with its own internal logic, cohesion axiomatised as adjunctions. He answers the intrinsic-geometry anchor by giving it universal, structural law. This is the same figure whose adjoint-unity was a neighbour of the metaphysics diagram; in the pendulum he sits cleanly at the mathematical form-pole, in productive tension with [mathematics-lautman] via [pendulum-poles-polemic] and discharged toward the working plane by [pendulum-verification].

Label: Riemann — intrinsic geometry as anchor
Description: Riemann read as the mathematics pendulum's immanent ground: the manifold specified by intrinsic local data — a metric given from within — with no ambient space to embed in or judge from. This is geometry that accounts for itself locally, the mathematical face of the same immanence Spinoza anchors in philosophy: the situation carries its own structure, and its tensions (curvature, singularity, the need for global coherence) drive the swing toward form and toward problem. [pendulum-formalization] carries it toward [mathematics-lawvere], [pendulum-problematization] toward [mathematics-lautman].

Label: the modal / cohesive homotopy-type-theory leg
Description: The formal-foundation side: contexts and their multiplicity of perspectives encoded as modal homotopy type theory — specifically the internal language of a cohesive (∞,1)-topos with its adjoint modalities (shape ⊣ flat ⊣ sharp). We follow Lawvere's axiomatic cohesion and the cohesive-HoTT of Schreiber–Shulman, with Corfield's *Modal Homotopy Type Theory* supplying the philosophical warrant for using it as a "logic of contexts". In the codebase this is the ModalHoTT development (currently paused at the de Rham named-coefficient stage). It supplies the left-hand site of [cross-site-adjunction].

Label: no-leak (unityping realised as a theorem)
Description: The framework's structural privacy guarantee, and the positive content behind the phrase "audit artifacts, never actors": the claim that the identity of an inquirer cannot leak across the runtime boundary, because that boundary is renaming-invariant. Formalised, renaming-invariance is univalence at the runtime boundary — equivalent actors are equal — which turns "unityping" from a stipulation into a theorem: no observation can distinguish two inquirers except through their typed contributions. We take it from `workflow/arc/12_correspondence_math_runtime.md` (its correspondence/realization discussion), with the provenance side in `workflow/arc/10_provenance_audit_layer.md`. "No-leak" is our plain-English image for the against-the-grain property that the trace records what was done without exposing who — by construction rather than by policy.

Label: no-privileged-actor theorem
Description: No-privileged-actor: system acceptance depends only on the typed trace and its proof obligations, not on the social identity or status of the inquirer — two unityped inquirers submitting equivalent moves with equivalent certificates are treated identically. This is one of the family's central anti-managerial results, and it folds in "role-erasure": any apparent authority reduces to a property of trace contributions rather than a primitive privilege. As a member of [protocol-theorems] it presupposes [no-leak], since identity must not leak for equal treatment to hold.

Label: Noether conservation as non-extractive work
Description: Noether's theorem read as the technical — not metaphorical — content of "borrow – work – give back": a continuous symmetry of the action yields a conserved current, so a transformation may rearrange a local region but must leave an invariant accounting through the boundary. A quantum anomaly is then a precise "failed giving-back": a classical symmetry that cannot be discharged consistently, which becomes a typed obstruction forcing a new context. This grounds the parallel between the framework and field theories at the level of conserved flow rather than analogy; it is a field-theoretic instance of [logic-as-contextual-transformation]. See `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: noninterference theorem
Description: Noninterference: metadata such as rank, prestige, institution, or identity label cannot affect a verification outcome unless explicitly typed as relevant evidence in the trace. It is the mechanically-checkable form of "social status cannot secretly influence acceptance", and it is essentially [no-leak] promoted from a property of the boundary to a property of the whole acceptance procedure. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is stronger than fairness rhetoric precisely because it is an invariant one can run a check against.

Label: normalization / redundancy theorem
Description: Normalization / redundancy: certain trace transformations can be simplified without changing their meaning or verified consequences — the trace analogue of proof normalization and cut-elimination. It is what lets duplicated arguments, unnecessary mediation, and bureaucratic clutter be compressed away, keeping the trace legible as it grows rather than accreting into an unreadable ledger. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is the maintenance theorem that keeps the other guarantees usable at scale.

Label: explicit-obstruction theorem
Description: Explicit obstruction: when local claims cannot be glued into a global one, the system produces an explicit obstruction object rather than failing silently — failed synthesis becomes typed knowledge. This is the constructive reading of contextuality (Abramsky) and descent-failure (Grothendieck): an impossibility is recorded as a thing that can be reasoned about and carried forward. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it supplies exactly what a legitimate context-extension must resolve, which is why [creativity-admissibility] depends on it.

Label: openness at both ends (no universal container)
Description: A standing constraint: the framework admits neither a greatest inner container (no "type of all types", resolved by a Grothendieck-style / Martin-Löf universe hierarchy) nor a completed outer totality (no topos of all toposes; the exterior it calls "reality" is never enclosed). These are the same refusal of self-collapse seen from two ends, and both are underwritten by [lawvere-diagonal]. The constraint is what lets the framework keep its metaphysical promise of no first instant and no final container. See `workflow/arc/11_reality.md`.

Label: anchor — the immanent ground
Description: The position an inquiry departs from and must ultimately account for without appeal to any outside judge: the immanent context or milieu taken as given at the start of a swing. It is not a foundation in the justificatory sense but the concrete situation whose own tensions drive the motion toward the two poles. [pendulum-formalization] carries it toward [pendulum-left] and [pendulum-problematization] toward [pendulum-right]; [pendulum-recontextualization] returns a fresh anchor to this position from [pendulum-equilibrium], closing the loop. Read as Spinoza in the philosophy instance and Riemann in the mathematics instance.

Label: equilibrium — the cared-for working balance
Description: Not a midpoint between the poles but an orthogonal working plane where their polemic is metabolised into an ongoing practice held in balance with care. It receives [pendulum-verification] from [pendulum-left] and [pendulum-stabilization] from [pendulum-right], and its closing move [pendulum-recontextualization] returns a new anchor to begin the next swing — making the whole shape recursive rather than terminal. Read as Peirce in philosophy and Grothendieck in mathematics; in the logic instance it is [workilibrium-logic] itself, the framework read as its own equilibrium.

Label: formalization (anchor → left)
Description: The invariant move that carries the immanent anchor toward the demand for form: taking a concrete situation and giving it intelligible structure, law, internal logic — the anchor answering its own tension on the side of the already-formed. Each instance realises it as a [realizes] edge from its anchor-reading to its left-pole-reading (Spinoza→Hegel in philosophy, Riemann→Lawvere in mathematics), carrying `relation: pendulum-formalization`.

Label: left pole — the demand for form
Description: The pole of intelligibility: the pull toward internal logic, law, settled structure, the already-formed — the side on which a situation is answered by being given form. It is reached from the anchor by [pendulum-formalization], held in irreducible tension with [pendulum-right] by [pendulum-poles-polemic], and discharged toward the working plane by [pendulum-verification]. Read as Hegel in philosophy and Lawvere in mathematics; in the logic instance it is the "demand for form" that the internal / formal logic expresses.

Label: poles-polemic (left ↔ right, paired)
Description: The paired tension between the two poles — form against novelty, law against genesis — that keeps neither able to absorb the other. It is not resolved at the pole-axis but only displaced into the orthogonal working plane; this productive antagonism is precisely what the equilibrium exists to metabolise. Each instance realises it as the left↔right edge (Hegel↔Deleuze, Lawvere↔Lautman), carrying `relation: pendulum-poles-polemic`.

Label: problematization (anchor → right)
Description: The invariant move that carries the immanent anchor toward the demand for novelty: eliciting from a situation its genetic problem, the generative excess that current form cannot yet capture — the anchor answering its tension on the side of the not-yet-formed. Each instance realises it as an anchor-reading → right-pole-reading edge (Spinoza→Deleuze, Riemann→Lautman), carrying `relation: pendulum-problematization`.

Label: recontextualization (equilibrium → anchor)
Description: The closing invariant move that returns the cared-for equilibrium as a fresh anchor for the next swing — the recursion that makes the pendulum a continuing practice rather than a one-shot resolution. It is the shape's core self-reference: the milieu, having accounted for itself, becomes the new immanent ground, which in the framework is the same recursion as [recursive-context-articulation]. Each instance realises it as an equilibrium-reading → anchor-reading edge (Peirce→Spinoza, Grothendieck→Riemann, read as a return that opens the next cycle), carrying `relation: pendulum-recontextualization`.

Label: right pole — the demand for novelty
Description: The pole of creativity: the pull toward genesis, the problem, the not-yet-formed, the generative source that exceeds current law. It is reached from the anchor by [pendulum-problematization], held in tension with [pendulum-left] via [pendulum-poles-polemic], and discharged toward the working plane by [pendulum-stabilization]. Read as Deleuze in philosophy and Lautman in mathematics; in the logic instance it is the "demand for novelty" that a genetic logic expresses.

Label: stabilization (right → equilibrium)
Description: The invariant move that discharges the right pole's novelty into the working plane: catching genesis before it dissipates and giving it enough hold to persist as practice, without freezing it back into mere law. Each instance realises it as a right-pole-reading → equilibrium-reading edge (Deleuze→Peirce, Lautman→Grothendieck), carrying `relation: pendulum-stabilization`.

Label: verification (left → equilibrium)
Description: The invariant move that discharges the left pole's form into the working plane: subjecting settled structure to the test of practice, so that intelligibility earns its place in the ongoing balance rather than ruling from above. Each instance realises it as a left-pole-reading → equilibrium-reading edge (Hegel→Peirce, Lawvere→Grothendieck), carrying `relation: pendulum-verification`.

Label: Deleuze — the demand for novelty
Description: Deleuze read at the right pole as the demand for novelty: affirmative difference, the virtual, and the genesis that exceeds any settled law — the pole where a problem generates its own solutions rather than receiving form from above. Localized complication (bracketed by the shape, kept here): in the *Logique du sens*, sense is a *surface* effect, not a depth-genesis, so reading Deleuze as pure generative depth flattens the surface/depth apparatus that lets sense be produced without being grounded. The pendulum reads him only through the novelty-demand and forgets this; noted here so the reading does not overclaim, and without adding any edge to the shape.

Label: Hegel — the demand for form
Description: Hegel read at the left pole as the demand for form: the labour of the concept, mediation-through-negation, the self-moving determination that answers the immanent ground by giving it intelligible structure. Localized complication (bracketed by the shape, kept here): in the *Science of Logic* the categories are not merely imposed form but *generate themselves* — a genesis-of-categories in which the "form pole" secretes its own content, so Hegel is not purely on the side of the already-formed. The pendulum reads him only through the form-demand and forgets this wrinkle; it is recorded here so the reading stays honest without leaking into the shape's invariant edges.

Label: the colimit of metaphysical neighbours
Description: A forcing-colimit, not a shape: the diagram of established metaphysical positions whose shared shape — "dépassement", in the arc's word — forces [recursive-context-articulation]. Hegel and Deleuze supply the seeding tension (mediation-through-negation versus affirmative difference), joined by Whitehead (process), Peirce (triadic semiosis), Simondon (individuation), Lautman and Zalamea (saturation/liberation as mathematical praxis), and Lawvere (adjoint unity-of-opposites, cohesion). Its job is derivational: the concept is positioned not as a new doctrine but as the shared shape into which each neighbour maps while keeping what matters, so the [recursive-context-articulation] `forced-by` edge into this node carries the graph's "why it is convincing". The [philosophy] pendulum is the *structured realization* of this colimit — it enriches the flat diagram with four positions and six invariant relations — but the two are kept distinct (see the schema's "shapes vs forcing-colimits"): the pendulum gives reading-structure, this node carries the forcing. Its inner-engine counterpart is [logic-neighbour-colimit].

Label: Peirce — the cared-for working balance
Description: Peirce read at the equilibrium as the cared-for working balance: triadic semiosis as an ongoing interpretive practice, fallibilism, the community of inquiry held together by agape — the "anti-managerial" care that lets independent inquirers stay independent (cf. [anchor-care]). This equilibrium plane is orthogonal to the Hegel–Deleuze pole-axis; it metabolises their polemic into a continuing practice rather than splitting the difference. Two neighbours the four positions do not name co-occupy this plane and are absorbed here rather than lost: Whitehead's process (reality as becoming-in-practice) and Simondon's individuation (the resolution of tensions into metastable structure). Its closing move [pendulum-recontextualization] returns a fresh anchor, which in the framework is [recursive-context-articulation].

Label: Spinoza — immanence as anchor
Description: Spinoza read as the philosophy pendulum's immanent ground: substance as immanent cause, a Nature that is its own explanation with no transcendent outside to judge it. This is why he anchors the shape — the pendulum's whole "no outside view" commitment is Spinozist immanence made into a starting milieu whose own tensions drive the swing toward form and toward novelty. The reading takes only this immanence-as-ground aspect; Spinoza's own necessitarianism and parallelism are left aside as not load-bearing for the position. [pendulum-formalization] carries this anchor toward [philosophy-hegel], [pendulum-problematization] toward [philosophy-deleuze].

Label: provenance theorem
Description: Provenance: every accepted claim has a finite dependency path back to its assumptions, data, definitions, rules, and prior accepted moves — nothing enters the trace without visible ancestry. This is the condition for trust without authority: a contribution is trustworthy because its lineage can be inspected, not because of who made it. It is a member of the [protocol-theorems] region and the ground on which [collective-memory] builds; the audit-layer detail lives in `workflow/arc/10_provenance_audit_layer.md`.

Label: the realization junction (Realization.agda)
Description: The point in the codebase where the two legs physically meet: a three-tier construction in which an audit table serves as a specification (tier 0), a generic Agda module instantiates the substrate carriers (tier 1), and theorems are transported across the boundary (tier 2). It is where [cross-site-adjunction] stops being a diagram and becomes running, type-checked code, and where renaming-invariance appears as univalence at the runtime boundary — the positive core of "no-leak". See `workflow/arc/12_correspondence_math_runtime.md` and the `RuntimeContract/Realization.agda` module.

Label: recursive context articulation
Description: The framework's core metaphysical pattern: a context generates a multiplicity of local perspectives; that multiplicity produces a language-and-type system that stabilises it; the stabilised system becomes a new context. It is a "process-semiotic" reading of reality — nearest neighbours Whitehead's process philosophy, Peirce's semiosis, Simondon's individuation — sharpened so that the third term is not merely "language" but a language paired with a constructive type theory. We adopt it from the dialogue recorded in `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`, where it is derived as the shared shape of a diagram of metaphysical neighbours (see [philosophy-neighbour-colimit]). Its one deliberate cost is that it posits no "first instant": every beginning is intelligible only as a local beginning within some context.

Label: responsibility theorem
Description: Responsibility: every accepted intervention carries a typed responsibility path — authoring, dependencies, known risks, repair obligations, and affected contexts — so responsibility follows transformations rather than offices. It is the trace-level realisation of the accountability back-edge from the praxis nexus, and it matters most where interventions are ecological, technical, or political and someone must be answerable. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is how "who is answerable" is derived from the work rather than assigned to a role.

Label: risk as the linear/conserved ambient base
Description: The reading of risk as the linear, conserved base over which the whole praxis nexus is enriched: because resources cannot be freely duplicated or discarded, every valued interaction is exposure, and risk is not an add-on but the ambient quantity the enrichment measures against. This is why trust and legitimacy have "cost" at all. It is a member of the [praxis-nexus] region and is the base underlying [enriched-completion-setting]. See `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`.

Label: the science pendulum (tentative seed)
Description: A deliberately provisional seed for a third instance of the [pendulum] shape, drawn over natural science and flagged as blurry — not yet earned. The tentative casting: an anchor of empirical immanence (Bacon–Galileo, the situation interrogated from within), a left pole of the demand for form (Newton–Einstein, law and unifying theory), a right pole of the demand for novelty (Darwin, genetic / evolutionary explanation), and an equilibrium of cared-for inquiry (Peirce again, the community of inquiry and fallibilist method — a distinct reading-node from [philosophy-peirce], since positions are shape-scoped). Unlike [philosophy] and [mathematics] this reading is unresolved: the pairings — especially compressing Newton and Einstein into one pole, and reusing Peirce across instances — are not settled, so it is recorded as a single seed node rather than built out into positions and edges. Its role is to test whether the shape generalises beyond philosophy and mathematics; if it holds, it becomes a full instance — acquiring a forcing-colimit only if a genuine neighbour-diagram argument later emerges, not as a matter of course.

Label: soundness theorem
Description: Soundness: nothing is accepted as formally verified unless there exists a checkable proof object for it under explicit assumptions — "accepted" never means "someone said so". It is the base guarantee of the [verification-layer] and the floor on which every other member of the [protocol-theorems] family stands, since provenance, auditability, and the anti-privilege results all assume that acceptance already tracks a real proof. Stated in `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.

Label: trace-sufficiency theorem (flagship)
Description: Trace-sufficiency, the flagship: every legitimate system decision factors through the typed trace, so the system never needs a privileged human authority outside the trace to justify acceptance, rejection, revision, merging, or repair. It is the formal heart of the project — "authority lives in the work, not the person" — and it presupposes [no-leak], without which the trace could not carry the whole of authority. It is held in explicit tension with [lawvere-diagonal], which forbids the trace from ever being a completed absolute: sufficient for every decision, yet never closed. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region.

Label: translation theorem
Description: Translation: a claim valid in one context can be transported to another only through an explicit translation preserving specified structure — "no context-smuggling". It is essential for interdisciplinary inquiry, where physical, economic, biological, and social languages cannot be casually interchanged without a typed bridge. A member of the [protocol-theorems] region, it is the theorem that makes cross-context reuse honest, and it is the natural home of a future `translates-to` edge drawn between two specific domain contexts once those are nodes.

Label: trust as an enriched hom-object
Description: The reading of trust as the enriched hom-object between inquirers: not a scalar reputation but the structured "distance" that lives in the enriching base, so that trust is the very thing an interaction is valued in. It is what has to be earned and is carried by the trace rather than by status. It is a member of the [praxis-nexus] region and is enriched over the conserved base [risk-linear-base]. See `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`.

Label: the mechanised verification layer
Description: The mechanised organ that discharges the formalisable part of inquiry — proof assistants (Lean, Coq, Agda) checking types, proofs, dependencies, and consistency-relative-to-assumptions — so that verification is a public operation on trace-objects rather than a privilege held by any person. It replaces "trust me, I checked it" with "here is the proof object; anyone can run the checker", which is the concrete anti-managerial move: it removes one whole source of hierarchy without installing a new one, provided the layer itself stays editable by the community. Drawn from `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`, it is the discharge step of [logic-as-contextual-transformation] turned into infrastructure — and the very thing [lawvere-diagonal] forbids from ever becoming a complete internal account of its own correctness.

Label: workilibrium — the logic pendulum's equilibrium
Description: A coined term (work + equilibrium) for the equilibrium position of the *logic* pendulum — and the single drawn member of a logic instance we have otherwise only seeded. Its firm point: the equilibrium of the logic pendulum is the Hoapa framework itself, read as its own cared-for working balance. The governing dyad is "return to equilibrium" (the context side — a milieu that must account for itself and be brought back into balance) crossed with "optimality of care" (the multiplicity side — [anchor-care]'s anti-managerial affect, which keeps independent inquirers independent). Work is primary: the equilibrium is something done and maintained, not a state inherited — trace and inheritance are *consequences* of the work, never its definition (reducing it to inheritance is degenerate, the way a parent who optimises for the bequest is a bad parent). The tentative anchor of this logic pendulum is "the immanent context" (the milieu with no outside judge); its poles fall out as the demand for form (internal / formal logic, [pendulum-left]) and the demand for novelty (genetic logic, [pendulum-right]). It concretely fills [pendulum-equilibrium] in the logic domain. The full logic instance and its forcing-colimit (the retained [logic-neighbour-colimit]) are left for later; workilibrium is the equilibrium seed around which they will be drawn — and note that the `forced-by` derivational edge must stay at that colimit level, not on this node alone.

Label: the five anchors
Description: The five commitments that pin [cross-site-adjunction] down to a specific adjunction rather than a formal analogy. Four locate its categorical parts — a left adjoint [anchor-complexity], a right adjoint [anchor-evolution], a unit [anchor-praxis], a counit [anchor-anthropic]; the fifth [anchor-care] is a transverse order-two structure. They share most of their external edges — each refines the same adjunction — but each also carries individual edges, and the region has internal structure. Treat the region as semi-autonomous: an edge whose target is `anchors` distributes to all five members unless a member individually overrides it.

Label: the mathematics pendulum
Description: A full instance of the [pendulum] shape drawn over mathematics: Riemann at [pendulum-anchor], Lawvere at [pendulum-left], Lautman at [pendulum-right], Grothendieck at [pendulum-equilibrium]. Unlike [philosophy] this instance is not the promotion of a pre-existing neighbour bag; it is a fresh reading that shows the same shape governing mathematical practice, and it is where two figures from the metaphysics neighbourhood (Lawvere, Lautman) find their proper home. Each figure is read through this shape's viewpoint only. The shape `instantiates → pendulum`; its equilibrium (Grothendieck's context-building "rising sea") is the mathematical exemplar of the framework's own [pendulum-equilibrium] — working the milieu into a cared-for balance from which the next problem is posed.

Label: the pendulum shape
Description: The pendulum is the general shape we use to read a domain of inquiry as a motion between two poles about an anchor, settling into a worked equilibrium — proposed as "the structure of the epistemology tag" for the whole framework. It declares four positions — [pendulum-anchor] (the immanent ground a domain departs from and must account for), [pendulum-left] (the demand for form, intelligibility, law), [pendulum-right] (the demand for novelty, genesis, problem), [pendulum-equilibrium] (the cared-for working balance a practice returns to) — and six invariant relations among them: [pendulum-formalization], [pendulum-problematization], [pendulum-poles-polemic], [pendulum-verification], [pendulum-stabilization], [pendulum-recontextualization]. As a template the shape is a pure set of these ten members; the directed skeleton lives in each operator's `from`/`to`. The load-bearing structural insight is that the equilibrium is *orthogonal* to the pole-axis — not a midpoint between left and right but a distinct working plane where the poles' polemic is metabolised into a practice, whose closing move ([pendulum-recontextualization]) hands a fresh anchor to the next swing, making the shape recursive rather than terminal. Two full instances draw it so far — [philosophy] and [mathematics], each `instantiates → pendulum` — while logic (its equilibrium seeded as [workilibrium-logic]) and science (the provisional [science-pendulum]) are only seeded, not yet built out into positions and edges.

Label: the philosophy pendulum
Description: A full instance of the [pendulum] shape drawn over modern metaphysics: Spinoza at [pendulum-anchor], Hegel at [pendulum-left], Deleuze at [pendulum-right], Peirce at [pendulum-equilibrium]. It is the structured promotion of what was recorded as a flat "diagram of metaphysical neighbours" — the shared shape into which those neighbours map — now given the pendulum's four places and six invariant relations rather than an unordered bag. The reading is deliberately partial: each figure is read *through this shape's viewpoint* (see the schema's "positions are readings, not properties"), so the local complications the shape brackets are carried inside the individual reading-nodes ([philosophy-hegel], [philosophy-deleuze]), and neighbours the four positions do not name (Whitehead's process, Simondon's individuation) are noted where they co-occupy a position. The shape `instantiates → pendulum`; its equilibrium→anchor loop is the framework's [recursive-context-articulation].

Label: the praxis nexus (trust, legitimacy, risk, accountability)
Description: The cluster in which the framework's "warm" practical vocabulary is recast as earned mathematical structure rather than sentiment: trust as an enriched hom [trust-enriched-hom], legitimacy as representability [legitimacy-representability], risk as a linear/conserved base [risk-linear-base], accountability as a dual back-edge [accountability-dual-edge]. (Care, the fifth term in the original discussion, lives in the [anchors] region as [anchor-care], since it is a condition on the community rather than something earned within it.) The members mutualise their setting — all live in [enriched-completion-setting] over the same base — but carry individual and internal edges. Treat the region as semi-autonomous, per the schema. See `workflow/arc/14_trust_and_legitimacy_as_enrichment.md`.

Label: the protocol-theorem family
Description: The family of theorems the typed verification layer is meant to yield — not statements about the world directly, but invariants of collective inquiry. Every member presupposes the [verification-layer] as its setting (a mutualised edge from the region), while individual members carry their own edges: the anti-privilege members to [no-leak], fork/merge safety to the Grothendieck trace-mathematics, responsibility to the accountability back-edge of the praxis nexus, creativity-admissibility to the creativity operator and the obstruction theorem. Its flagship is [trace-sufficiency]: every legitimate decision factors through the typed trace. Treat the region as semi-autonomous per the schema; derived in `workflow/arc/15_metaphysics_and_logic.md`.
